name: three-d-sample-at-the-near-face-of-a-four-slice-texture
rationale: The fragment builds its 3D coordinate as (uv.x, uv.y, 0) and the texture is one texel wide and tall, so the interpolated uv cannot reach a second texel and only the depth axis decides the answer; the four slices are distinct exact halves and clamp-to-edge puts the third coordinate on slice zero.

name: constant-zero-position-observation
no_effect: Every clip position is zero (w = 0): the primitive covers no fragment, so the render target keeps its authored bytes. The zero position is a constant of the function, so no input makes the primitive cover a fragment: the family has no computing variant.
rationale: Every invocation returns float4(0) as clip position. The typed position observer is attached, but the degenerate zero-w primitive produces no fragments, so the exact one-pixel framebuffer observation remains the authored poison bytes.

name: matmul2d-bfloat-sum-order-nn-right-cooperative
rationale: The order of matmul2d's float sums (DESIGN D272): 16x16x32, transpose_right false, multiply_accumulate, bfloat A and B (B in cooperative memory, filled by coordinate), float cooperative destination, function constant 0 = 8; 14 threadgroups of 32 threads, threadgroup t computing out[256 t + 16 m + n] from the blocks tiles[t] names. Tiles: 6 column-pair tiles (A all 2^15; column n of B holds 2^15 at k = i_n, -2^15 at k = j_n, 2^-14 elsewhere, so products are +-2^30 and 2: the result counts, in 2s, the small products the sum adds after the pair cancels; pairs (0, j), (i, i + 1), (i, 31), C zero); 2 row-pair tiles (the same with row m of A holding the pair (0, j), B all 2^15); 2 C-position tiles (C = 2^30, column n of B holds -2^15 at k = n or 16 + n: the result counts the small products added after C meets that product); 4 random tiles (8-bit significands, magnitudes 2^-6 to 2^7, either sign, every value exact in the element type). Output words never written keep 0xDEADBEEF. Metal's answer is a measurement; the candidate matches it exactly only if it sums in Metal's order. Loops bounded by the capacity.

name: gather-depth-quad-lands-inside-one-uniform-block
rationale: The kernel is straight-line, so execution_safety is loop_free. It gathers the depth texture at pixel coordinate index*2 through a constexpr sampler that reflection reports as coord::pixel, nearest/nearest, clamp_to_edge, and reduces the four texels to float4(min, max, count_below_one, 4). The destination is texture2d<float, write>, which types as R32f, so only the min is observable; dstSize carries air.arg_unused and is never read. The input is four uniform 4x4 blocks -- 0.5 top-left, 0.25 top-right, 0.75 bottom-left, 1.0 bottom-right -- and the case reads back exactly one output texel, (1, 1), whose gather coordinate is (2, 2). Every 2x2 footprint a gather can take around (2, 2) lies inside {1,2,3}^2, so it stays within the top-left block under any of the conventions for which quad a pixel-coordinate gather selects, and min is exactly 0.5 without the case having to assert one of them. What the single value does pin is the addressing: treating the coordinate as normalized would clamp (2, 2) to the far corner and give 1.0, reducing over the whole texture would give 0.25, and being four texels off in either axis would give 0.25 or 0.75. All four block values are exact in binary32 and in depth32_float, so nothing rests on rounding.

name: anchor-three-transcendentals-where-rounding-cannot-reach
rationale: Five uncovered families -- air.rsqrt.v3f32 (4 corpus sources), air.log2.v3f16 (4), air.cospi.f16 (4), air.simd_sum.v4f32 (3) and air.simd_shuffle_up.s.i16 (3) -- all asked only where the answer is exactly representable, so every word is a derivation rather than a recording. Each rsqrt argument is a power of four, so the answer is a power of two; that is the guard that matters, because the fast_ roots on this host are not correctly rounded and an exactly representable ANSWER alone does not pin one. log2 sees only powers of two and cospi only integers, where the answer is exactly +-1 -- at odd half-integers Metal returns -0 where MoltenVK returns +0, a signed-zero divergence out of the argument reduction, so those arguments are deliberately not asked. simd_sum is association-proof by construction: every lane contributes an integer and the column totals (528 and 48) are far below 2^24, so any accumulation order gives the same bits, while the lane values still differ enough that summing the wrong set cannot match. simd_shuffle_up with delta 3 leaves the three lowest lanes undefined and those slots are overwritten on a branch over tid, never over the shuffle result. All 288 words were derived in Python before the GPU was asked.

name: every-iteration-reads-the-word-loaded-before-the-loop-not-the-loops-own-stores
rationale: One thread loads v = values[slots[count]] = values[0] = 7 before a loop of count = 6 iterations, and iteration i stores v * (i + 2) to values[slots[i]], slots = 0 1 0 2 0 3 (slots[6] = 0), so it stores over values[0] three times; values starts as 7, 100, 200, 300, then 0xffffffff in words 4 to 7. Metal reads v once: the words end as 42, 21, 35, 49, 4294967295, 4294967295, 4294967295, 4294967295. A translation whose loop reads values[0] again (MoltenVK 1.4.1's SPIRV-Cross forwards the load into the loop, DESIGN D453 item 3) multiplies the earlier stores instead: 336, 42, 280, 2352, 4294967295, 4294967295, 4294967295, 4294967295. v is read once per iteration and whole, so SPIRV-Cross has no second read that would make it declare v before the loop on its own. The loaded element, the slots and the trip count come from buffers, so the compiler can neither forward a store to the load, keep the stores in registers, nor unroll the loop.

name: imageblock-extent-queried-from-every-cell
rationale:
air.get_imageblock_width and air.get_imageblock_height, 17 corpus sources each and both uncovered. Every one of the 256 threads asks for both, so a lowering that answered only for the first cell, or that took the answer from the thread position instead of the tile, would show up in 255 of the 256 rows.

The imageblock is 16 by 16, the same extent as the threadgroup -- which is the only shape Metal accepts for an implicit imageblock, and the reason the two queries can be answered from the kernel's local size at all. Both answers are 16, and the two are deliberately equal only because Metal will not take a non-square tile here; the two remaining slots are red and blue of the tile cell the thread owns, red carrying the column and blue the row times sixteen plus the column, so a transposed or mis-strided tile moves them even though the extents cannot.

name: linked-single-unit-reduce-argmin
rationale: One invocation reduces one float element and writes its zero index. Reduction, broadcast, minor, major, outer-axis, per-thread, and NDArray extents and strides are one, bounding every loop to the single authored value.

name: fragment-implicit-level-of-detail-walks-a-five-level-rgba32-float-2d
rationale: TODO 6.2, DESIGN D351 item 2: sampler.sample_implicit, a fragment function's sample with neither level nor bias, over a 16x16 rgba32_float texture whose five levels each hold one distinct value. The q-th 2x2 quad along x of the 10x2 target scales its pixel position by 2^q / 16, so the coordinate's derivatives are exactly 2^q texels per pixel on both axes and the level of detail is exactly q (0 to 4); with a nearest mip filter each quad reads level q, and the output is exact on every device.

name: kernel-sample-bias-selects-a-level-of-a-five-level-rgba32-float-2d
rationale: TODO 6.2, DESIGN D351 item 2: sampler.sample_base_level, a kernel's sample with a bias and no level, over a 16x16 rgba32_float texture whose five levels each hold one distinct value. Metal reads level 0 shifted by the bias; with a nearest mip filter each thread's bias (whole levels, quarter-way between them, below 0 and past the last level) names one level, so the output is that level's value and is exact on every device.

name: linked-single-element-write
rationale: One dispatched invocation addresses a single authored NDArray element. The reference-size function constant makes one address-table slot available, the mapping constant assigns distinct x/y/z/w lanes, every dimension and stride is one, and the linked callbacks contain no loops. The prefix returns exact one and the postfix writes that value to the selected element.

name: linked-single-invocation-zero-bin
rationale: One invocation is bounded by source_size 1x1. Linking is enabled with one authored texture and one address-table element; the exact callback is loop-free and returns float4 zero without dereferencing either resource. The one-bin histogram parameters force every active scalar lane to bin zero, and the poisoned counter makes the bounded global-atomic write observable byte-exactly.

name: control-point-and-patch-input-fetches-past-their-buffers
rationale: Four triangle patches of three control points over eight control-point elements and two patch-input elements: control points 8 to 11 and patch inputs 2 and 3 are fetched past their buffers (DESIGN D258). Metal's fetch is unchecked, so the oracle binds both buffers with 16-byte shadows and records zero for the words they feed; the candidate pulls both with D10's check or the device's buffer robustness.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-five-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 5 and receives exact float4 zero from all four linked _uber_clear bodies. A seven-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry swizzles it to float4(0,0,0,1), writes both required poisoned output textures, and captures binding zero byte-exactly.

name: constant-uint-render-target
rationale: The parameter-free fragment entry returns the constant uint value 255 to color attachment zero; a generated full-coverage triangle must replace the poisoned one-pixel R32Uint target with that exact word.

name: sign-of-the-l1-residual-scaled-by-lambda
rationale: One invocation with pixel_index 0, so the predict stride multiplies to zero and every buffer is read at element 0 whatever stride says. predict (5, 1, 2) minus truth (1, 3, 6) is the residual (4, -2, -4), and air.sign.v3f32 of it is (1, -1, -1) exactly: sign has no approximation freedom, it selects one of three representable constants, so the comparison is exact whatever recompiles the module. lambda_l1 is 0.5, so dL1_drgb holds (0.5, -0.5, -0.5). Every lane is authored a different magnitude before the sign (4, 2, 4 apart from their signs), so a lowering that forwards the residual, takes its absolute value, or negates it changes the bytes; the lane pattern (+, -, -) is not a palindrome, so reversing the lanes changes them too. No residual lane is zero: the entry carries no-signed-zeros-fp-math, which licenses either zero for sign(0), so a zero lane would be authoring on a value the attribute leaves free rather than on the operation. The companion accum_losses output uses air.fast_fabs.v3f32 on the same residual and is left unobserved.

name: a-kernel-resets-a-compute-and-a-render-command-the-host-encoded
rationale: Kernel resets (DESIGN D336) of commands the host encoded. The host encodes three compute commands (each a dispatch of 64 threads in groups of 8 of the compute template, token 1, inherited: out[tid] = params[0] * (tid + 1) + params[1], with a 32-byte threadgroup length; command k binding the params and out windows k at 256 * k bytes) and two render commands (each a draw of 4 points, 2 instances, of the render template, token 2, inherited: out[16 * iid + vid] = params[0] * (vid + 1) + params[1] + 1000 * iid; command k binding windows 3 + k). Producer thread 0 resets compute command 1 and thread 1 render command 0, so neither runs: windows 1 and 3 keep the 0xab fill. Window 0 (scale 5, bias 10) holds 5 * (t + 1) + 10 at words t < 64, window 2 (scale 3, bias 1) 3 * (t + 1) + 1 at words 128 + t, and window 4 (scale 9, bias 5) 9 * (vid + 1) + 5 + 1000 * iid at words 256 + 16 * iid + vid for vid < 4, iid < 2. Every other word keeps the 0xab fill.
